input.rationale: A prose claim in the knowledge index became citable at no cost: the entry that says the incumbent answered neither the pre-vote nor the vote request already named the receipt it came from, and that receipt contains the two events that witness it. I added indices 12 and 16 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568 to the entry's executions and left its statement, conditions and sources untouched, so the claim that the lease suppressed both requests is now backed by the two events that record responded=false on the incumbent, rather than resting on the wording of the entry. I checked both indices against the receipt before citing them and they are the events the sentence describes: q_prevote_at_incumbent and q_vote_at_incumbent, each with node 1 and responded false.

knowledge.statement: In a three-voter group, one peer-form MsgForgetLeader delivered to the single other voter (node 2) is enough for a candidate whose log equals that voter's log to win the pre-vote, win the real vote and become StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent node 1 still reports StateLeader at term 2; the incumbent answered neither the pre-vote nor the vote request (its own lease suppressed both), and once the leader's next real heartbeat was processed the follower's context was restored and the identical pre-vote was ignored again.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 5-8 and 13-18 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568; config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum+PreVote, voters {1,2,3} with a shared log at index=10/term=1 in the storage snapshot. Correction of an earlier premise: the term-2 entry appended by leader 1 was not replicated to the followers by this harness (a later native run of the extended harness shows the new leader appending with prev=(index=10, term=1)), so that entry was uncommitted and no part of any comparison here depends on it; the incumbent was not fed the new leader's messages, so its demotion path is outside this observation; no follower was ticked, so follower election timeouts did not fire.

knowledge.statement: IsLocalMsg returns true only for MsgHup, MsgBeat, MsgUnreachable, MsgSnapStatus, MsgCheckQuorum, MsgStorageAppend, MsgStorageAppendResp, MsgStorageApply and MsgStorageApplyResp; MsgForgetLeader (MessageType 23) is therefore classified as a network message, and RawNode.Step rejects a message only when IsLocalMsg(m.Type) && !IsLocalMsgTarget(m.From), returning ErrStepLocalMsg otherwise delivering it to raft.Step.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot; classification is by MessageType only, independent of From/To and of any term field; node.Step has the same predicate and silently ignores local types received from a non-local sender.

knowledge.statement: No code path in the snapshot sends, forwards or replicates MsgForgetLeader: its only producers are RawNode.ForgetLeader and node.ForgetLeader, which call raft.Step directly, and stepFollower acts on it locally by setting r.lead=None (refusing when ReadOnlyOption is ReadOnlyLeaseBased); a message with Term==0 is classified as a local message by Step and skips all term comparisons.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot; grep over the whole tree shows MsgForgetLeader only in rawnode.go, node.go, raftpb (enum/aliases), rafttest handlers and no r.send/message-construction site.

knowledge.statement: In Step, a MsgVote or MsgPreVote with a higher term is ignored (no response at all) when force is false and inLease holds, where inLease := checkQuorum && lead != None && electionElapsed < electionTimeout; a follower that has lead==None fails inLease and instead evaluates canVote, where the third clause (m.Type == MsgPreVote && m.Term > r.Term) holds for a pre-vote from any node, so an up-to-date candidate is granted.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot; requires Config.CheckQuorum and a leader context (lead != None) established by a recent real leader message; the retained interaction expectation testdata/forget_leader_prevote_checkquorum.txt documents the same intent for the operator-driven local API.

knowledge.statement: With three real RawNode instances in one process (voters {1,2,3}, CheckQuorum+PreVote, shared log at index=10/term=1), delivering a message of type MsgForgetLeader with From=3, To=2 and no term field through RawNode.Step returns no error, sets the follower's SoftState.Lead from 1 to 0, and makes that follower answer the same real MsgPreVote (term 3 from an up-to-date candidate) that it had ignored while the lease held: the first delivery produced no response message at all, the delivery after the forged message produced a MsgPreVoteResp with Reject=false.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 3 and 5 of CheckRun ebe1baaa4adf43c5bb6b067dc7c4a5c7 (events prevote_outcome under_lease / after_forget), with the admission events heartbeat_delivered (index 0) and inbound_forget_leader (index 4) in the same runner stream; the follower was never ticked between measurements, so its election-timer lease was active; control at index 2 shows a genuinely local type (MsgCheckQuorum) from the same sender is still rejected with ErrStepLocalMsg.

knowledge.statement: Repeating the peer-form MsgForgetLeader once per heartbeat round keeps a follower from enforcing the leader lease: over three consecutive rounds the leader's real heartbeat restored the follower's leader context (lead 0 -> 1) and the accepted message cleared it again (1 -> 0), and the identical retried pre-vote from an up-to-date candidate was granted in every round, while the leader remained StateLeader at term 2 throughout.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 29, 32, 33, 35, 36 and 38 of CheckRun fda749eb6eb64986a3bd5e9a0c950849; config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum+PreVote, voters {1,2,3} from equal storage snapshots at index=10/term=1; only the leader is ticked, so follower election timeouts never fire; the candidate's pre-vote request is reused unchanged as a retry and its grant is not fed back.

knowledge.statement: A real raft.Node with id 2 started by RestartNode, whose reported leader was set to 1 by delivering a real leader heartbeat through Node.Step, had that leader cleared to 0 by delivering a peer-form MsgForgetLeader (From=3, To=2, no term field) through the same Node.Step, with no error returned; Node.ForgetLeader on the same node produced the identical state change, and a genuinely local type (MsgCheckQuorum) delivered from a peer through Node.Step left the leader unchanged.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 41, 42 and 43 of CheckRun 89b72b31226944e1b1175a08c2746c40; config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum+PreVote, voters {1,2,3} from equal storage snapshots at index=10/term=1; values are read from Node.Status (synchronized with the node's run loop by polling until the expected value appears, poll count reported as 0 at index 41 and 42); the node's Ready stream was drained by a goroutine calling Advance.

knowledge.statement: Both intended producers of MsgForgetLeader bypass the inbound filter rather than depending on it: RawNode.ForgetLeader calls raft.Step directly, and node.ForgetLeader uses the internal step path that sends the message to the receive channel instead of Node.Step. Classifying MsgForgetLeader as a local message would therefore leave both APIs working (their messages never pass IsLocalMsg) while making RawNode.Step return ErrStepLocalMsg and Node.Step ignore messages of that type received from a peer.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only: no execution is claimed for this statement. It follows from src_rawnode_forget (direct raft.Step call), src_nodestep (the Step filter that node.ForgetLeader does not use) and src_forgetdoc (the API that applications are meant to call), together with src_islocal (the filter predicate itself).

knowledge.statement: MsgForgetLeader is the only message type in the enum whose producers are purely local and yet is absent from isLocalMsg. Sweeping the enum against the filter and producer sites: MsgHup, MsgBeat, MsgCheckQuorum, MsgUnreachable, MsgSnapStatus, MsgStorageAppend, MsgStorageAppendResp, MsgStorageApply and MsgStorageApplyResp are all locally produced and all listed; MsgProp, MsgApp, MsgAppResp, MsgVote, MsgVoteResp, MsgSnap, MsgHeartbeat, MsgHeartbeatResp, MsgTransferLeader, MsgTimeoutNow, MsgReadIndex, MsgReadIndexResp, MsgPreVote and MsgPreVoteResp are produced for or forwarded over the network and correctly unlisted; MsgForgetLeader is produced only by the two local ForgetLeader APIs and is unlisted, so it is the single exception.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution is claimed): the enum in raftpb, the isLocalMsg array in util.go, and every construction site for MsgForgetLeader found by searching the tree (rawnode.go, node.go, and the rafttest handlers, none of which put it on the wire). This bounds the earlier finding: the omission is a single-point classification gap, not a pattern.

knowledge.statement: A leader that stops hearing from a quorum steps down by itself: tickHeartbeat fires a MsgCheckQuorum step every election timeout when Config.CheckQuorum is set, and stepLeader responds to MsgCheckQuorum by calling ProgressTracker.QuorumActive (which treats each non-learner's RecentActive flag, reset for every peer but itself after each check, as a vote) and becoming a follower when that quorum is not active. So in a CheckQuorum deployment the coexistence of the incumbent and a leader elected at a higher term is bounded by an election timeout of the incumbent's own logical clock, not by how long the new leader's messages take to arrive.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution is claimed): raft.go 862-880 (tickHeartbeat's election-timeout branch dispatching MsgCheckQuorum), raft.go 1281-1294 (stepLeader's MsgCheckQuorum arm stepping down and clearing RecentActive for every peer but itself) and tracker/tracker.go 205-218 (QuorumActive over the voters' RecentActive flags) (set true on any peer message, cleared for all peers but the leader at each check). Applies only when Config.CheckQuorum is enabled; the bound was not measured in any receipt of this run, so it constrains the earlier receipts' scope rather than being witnessed by them.

knowledge.statement: A leader elected by a real vote among three equal-log voters, then advanced 20 ticks with no message delivered in either direction, was already StateFollower at the first CheckQuorum check (tick 10, its election timeout) and still a follower at tick 20, with its term unchanged at 2 throughout - so the module's own quorum check, not a peer's higher term, ended the leadership and it did so within one election timeout.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 45 and 46 of CheckRun 4393d47e3d51423390832c2b3d736512 (event s_leader_state at ticks=10 and ticks=20), with the pre-check state at the same receipt's s_leader_before event (ticks=0, StateLeader, term 2); config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum=true, PreVote=true, voters {1,2,3} from equal storage snapshots at index=10/term=1; nothing was delivered to the leader after the election, so this measures the silent case only.

knowledge.statement: A MsgReadIndex received by a leader that has not committed an entry in its own term is appended to pendingReadIndexMessages and answered only through releasePendingReadIndexMessages, which is called from a single site - the leader's append-response path once commit progress releases the queue - and which first requires committedEntryInCurrentTerm, otherwise it logs an error and leaves the queue intact. No other code path writes or clears the field: the search over the tree finds only the field declaration, the queueing site and that helper with its one call site, so a request queued before the node loses leadership is never cancelled; it is answered only if the same node again becomes leader and commits in a later term, in which case it is answered with the commit index reached at release time, and it otherwise stays unanswered.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution claimed): field declaration raft.go 428-435, queueing at raft.go 1361-1368, the release helper at raft.go 2127-2143 and its single call at raft.go 1548-1556. The caller contract that makes the unanswered case acceptable is node.go 218-224 (ReadIndex: 'request can be lost without notice, therefore it is user's job to ensure read index retries'). Not a defect finding; recorded because it bounds what the module guarantees about completion of an accepted read duty, and because a caller that assumed otherwise would retry unnecessarily - or not at all.

knowledge.statement: A leader elected with its append acknowledgement withheld has no commit in its own term, and a ReadIndex request issued then is accepted without producing any read state; once the follower receives that append and its acknowledgement is returned, the leader's commit advances to that index (with matches {1:11, 3:11} out of voters {1,2,3}) and the queued request is released as a read state carrying the index reached at release time and the original request context.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 48, 49 and 50 of CheckRun d7a20d42d5b84569a0c6e4924cd577a9; config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum+PreVote, ReadOnlySafe, voters {1,2,3} from equal storage snapshots at index=10/term=1, with node 2 never contacted so the quorum is exactly the leader plus node 3; the harness delivery helper writes each Ready's HardState and Entries to that node's MemoryStorage before Advance, which is the application duty the Ready contract states and without which this path cannot complete.

knowledge.statement: A read request queued by a leader that has no commit in its own term is not answered while that node loses leadership: after its own quorum check demoted it to follower at its old term, no read state had appeared for the request it still owed, and nothing answered it while it was not leader. When the same node led again at a higher term and committed an entry there, the stale request was released with the read index committed at that release time (12, where the index recorded at acceptance was 10) and with the request context it was accepted with.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 52 and 54 of CheckRun 478561f525b3471ca92b9aa20c6d12df; config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum+PreVote, ReadOnlySafe, voters {1,2,3} from equal snapshots at index=10/term=1 with node 2 never contacted; the demotion came from the node's own CheckQuorum check, and the harness writes Ready entries to storage before Advance.

knowledge.statement: The regression is transient and self-healing. MaybeDecrTo's non-replicate branch lowers Next to max(min(rejected, matchHint+1), Match+1) and clears MsgAppFlowPaused, but while the progress is in StateSnapshot (a) the reject path in stepLeader calls BecomeProbe only for StateReplicate, so the state is unchanged, and (b) sendAppend returns immediately because IsPaused is true for StateSnapshot, so nothing is sent from the regressed value. Both ways out of StateSnapshot recompute Next from PendingSnapshot: a MsgSnapStatus without a rejection calls BecomeProbe with Next = max(Match+1, PendingSnapshot+1), and one with a rejection first zeroes PendingSnapshot and then calls BecomeProbe with Next = Match+1. So a stale rejection in that state at most logs a decrement, and the snapshot outcome restores a consistent Next; no probe from the wrong index and no stall follows.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution claimed): MaybeDecrTo at tracker/progress.go 226-261, BecomeProbe at 130-152, IsPaused at 262-278, the reject path at raft.go 1505-1520 and MsgSnapStatus handling at 1611-1624. The reachable trigger is a rejection for an append the leader sent before entering StateSnapshot, which under this source is the only way MaybeDecrTo sees rejected == Next-1 there.

knowledge.statement: The application-facing ordering duties are enforced by fatal guards, not by clamping: appending entries whose predecessor is below the commit index panics, committing to an index past the last index panics, reporting an applied index outside [previously applied, committed] panics, accepting application for an index past committed panics, and computing a non-positive application size budget panics. The only tolerated adjustments are non-fatal: applied-to bookkeeping clamps its outstanding-size counter at zero, and application is paused (applyingEntsPaused) once the outstanding size reaches the configured limit, resuming when the application's acknowledgement, via Applied or the storage apply response, brings the outstanding size down. Entry rewriting above the commit index is allowed by design, which is how a follower replaces a divergent uncommitted tail.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution claimed): log.go 136-140 (append guard), 322-328 (commitTo guard), 330-341 (appliedTo guard and counter clamp), 344-356 (acceptApplying guard and the pause condition), 234-238 (budget guard), with the client duties stated in node.go around ReadIndex/Ready and in the Ready struct documentation. The guards fire on values the module itself passes (from Ready/Advance) as well as on values an application reports in MsgStorageApplyResp, so a misreporting application is the party that trips them.

knowledge.statement: Step skips all term handling for a message whose term is zero, treating it as a local message, and then dispatches on its type: for MsgApp, MsgHeartbeat and MsgSnap that reaches stepFollower, which sets the election timer to zero and adopts m.From as the leader before handling the payload. So term-zero trust is not specific to MsgForgetLeader; what is specific to it is that it is the only locally-produced type missing from the inbound filter, so it reaches that trust from a peer with no illegal field at all, while a peer would have to send MsgApp or MsgHeartbeat with an illegal zero term to reach the same state change. That illegal-term path is not a correct-peer behaviour, its effect is bounded (a follower's advertised leader and timer, with a divergent uncommitted tail that the next real leader truncates) and it needs no classification change to be described.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution claimed): raft.go 1094-1100 (the term switch whose first case is the local-message case) and 1730-1739 (stepFollower setting electionElapsed and lead for MsgApp, MsgHeartbeat and MsgSnap). The contrast assumes a follower already at a term of at least 1, which every node reaches through becomeFollower(1, None) before it can lead or vote; the finding it clarifies is the main question's, whose evidence is the receipts cited there.

knowledge.statement: With a live leader already established from follower 2's point of view, a MsgHeartbeat from node 1 set its reported leader to 1, and a MsgHeartbeat of the same type from node 3 with no term field at all was accepted with no error and set the reported leader to 3; the follower therefore adopted a peer as leader on the strength of an illegal (unset) term rather than of a higher term.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 56 and 57 of CheckRun 2bb2e787750a4a799620f0b0d1673692 (event t_control_heartbeat with lead_after 1, and t_term0_heartbeat with term 0, step_error empty and lead_after 3, with the admission event t_setup carrying node 2, StateFollower, term 2, lead 0); voters {1,2,3} from equal snapshots at index=10/term=1 with CheckQuorum+PreVote, delivery through RawNode.Step, and the helper writing Ready entries to storage before Advance. The message is deliberately illegal for a peer to send: no correct producer emits a network-type message with the optional term field unset.

knowledge.statement: A peer-form MsgForgetLeader carrying a well-formed term acts exactly like the term-less form. With three real RawNodes (voters {1,2,3}, CheckQuorum+PreVote, equal logs at index=10/term=1) and follower 2 holding a live leader context at term 2, delivering MsgForgetLeader with From=3, To=2 and Term=2 through RawNode.Step returned no error and set SoftState.Lead from 1 to 0 (index 61 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624); the identical pre-vote from the up-to-date candidate that the lease had withheld immediately before was granted immediately after (index 62), while the leader's real heartbeat had left Lead at 1 (index 59) and the same pre-vote under that live lease had produced no response at all (index 60).
knowledge.conditions: Follower is a voter holding a live leader context at the same term as the delivered message; sender is a real voter; Config.CheckQuorum and PreVote set; ReadOnlyOption is not ReadOnlyLeaseBased; the message is handed to RawNode.Step directly.

knowledge.statement: Step's term switch has cases only for a zero term, a higher term and a lower term, so a message whose term equals the receiver's own passes the whole term switch untouched and reaches the switch on its type; MsgForgetLeader has no case there either, so control lands in the default dispatch r.step(r, m), which for a follower is stepFollower, where the type sets r.lead = None whenever a leader is recorded and refuses only under ReadOnlyLeaseBased. The leader context is therefore cleared at the term the follower already holds, with no term comparison and no error, so the acceptance is a property of the missing classification rather than of the term field.
knowledge.conditions: Receiver is a follower; message type MsgForgetLeader; message term equals the receiver's own term or is zero; sender id is not checked for membership; ReadOnlyOption != ReadOnlyLeaseBased.

knowledge.statement: The snapshot's own tests do not pin IsLocalMsg(MsgForgetLeader) in either direction, and its inbound-path tests cannot detect a type missing from the filter. TestIsLocalMsg (util_test.go) enumerates every message type in the enum except one, listing all 23 types from MsgHup through MsgStorageApplyResp (the type numbered 22), and the single type every one of those entries omits is MsgForgetLeader, the last-numbered type (23). TestRawNodeStep steps a message of every type in MessageType_name through the real RawNode.Step and asserts ErrStepLocalMsg only when IsLocalMsg(msgt) is already true. TestNodeStep routes every type through the public node.Step and expects the receive channel to stay empty only when IsLocalMsg(msgt) is already true. Both tests read their expectation from the table under test, so neither would fail today for MsgForgetLeader, and neither would fail if the type were classified as local.
knowledge.conditions: Read from the captured snapshot as expectations, not executed in this run. RawNode.Step rejects a local-typed message with ErrStepLocalMsg when the sender is not a local thread id, whereas the public node.Step silently returns nil after ignoring it; the internal node.step path that node.ForgetLeader uses never passes through that check, which is why the two producers keep working either way.

knowledge.statement: The CheckQuorum leader lease is skipped when an incoming vote request carries the CampaignTransfer context marker. In Step, a MsgVote or MsgPreVote with a term higher than the receiver's own is ignored only when force is false and inLease holds, where force := bytes.Equal(m.GetContext(), []byte(campaignTransfer)) and inLease := checkQuorum && lead != None && electionElapsed < electionTimeout; with the marker present the receiver advances to the higher term and then evaluates canVote and isUpToDate, so a lease that is otherwise live suppresses nothing. The module attaches the marker only for a transfer campaign: campaign() sets Context = []byte(campaignTransfer) on every MsgVote request when t == campaignTransfer, the path reached from stepFollower's MsgTimeoutNow case, which calls r.hup(campaignTransfer); that campaign increments the term, sends MsgVote rather than MsgPreVote at the new term, and is the only producer of the marker. The receiving node keeps no local record of a pending transfer, so it cannot tell a real transfer from a claimed one; the marker is a statement about an internal precondition of the sender rather than about anything the receiver can verify.
knowledge.conditions: Config.CheckQuorum must be set, otherwise inLease is always false and the lease suppresses nothing; the receiver must be a follower holding a live leader context inside its election timeout; the marker only matters for MsgVote or MsgPreVote whose term exceeds the receiver's own; ReadOnlyOption is not involved.

result.summary: Turned a prose claim in the knowledge index into a citable one. The entry that states the incumbent answered neither the pre-vote nor the vote request already named the receipt it came from, and that same receipt contains the two events that witness it, so I added indices 12 and 16 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568 — q_prevote_at_incumbent and q_vote_at_incumbent, each recording node 1 with responded false — to the entry's executions. I verified both indices against the receipt before citing them; they are exactly the two events the sentence describes, so the claim that the lease suppressed both requests now rests on recorded witnesses rather than on the wording of the entry. The statement, conditions and sources are unchanged, and the only changed field is executions, which keeps the update honest about what moved. This also closes a small gap that the correction earlier this run made visible: I had learned to distrust a bare responded flag, and here the same pair of flags is the evidence for the opposite conclusion, which is only sound because the entry's claim is about the absence of a response and the flags record exactly that. Nothing else was touched, submission validates with execution_requested=false, and the record still has no uncited executions.

knowledge.statement: In a three-voter group, one peer-form MsgForgetLeader delivered to the single other voter (node 2) is enough for a candidate whose log equals that voter's log to win the pre-vote, win the real vote and become StateLeader at term 3 while the incumbent node 1 still reports StateLeader at term 2; the incumbent answered neither the pre-vote nor the vote request (its own lease suppressed both), and once the leader's next real heartbeat was processed the follower's context was restored and the identical pre-vote was ignored again.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 5-8 and 13-18 of CheckRun 4ff9bf25cb164dd8bcf9d3be02aa1568; config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum+PreVote, voters {1,2,3} with a shared log at index=10/term=1 in the storage snapshot. knowledge.statement: Both intended producers of MsgForgetLeader bypass the inbound filter rather than depending on it: RawNode.ForgetLeader calls raft.Step directly, and node.ForgetLeader uses the internal step path that sends the message to the receive channel instead of Node.Step. Classifying MsgForgetLeader as a local message would therefore leave both APIs working (their messages never pass IsLocalMsg) while making RawNode.Step return ErrStepLocalMsg and Node.Step ignore messages of that type received from a peer.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only: no execution is claimed for this statement. It follows from src_rawnode_forget (direct raft.Step call), src_nodestep (the Step filter that node.ForgetLeader does not use) and src_forgetdoc (the API that applications are meant to call), together with src_islocal (the filter predicate itself).

knowledge.statement: MsgForgetLeader is the only message type in the enum whose producers are purely local and yet is absent from isLocalMsg. Sweeping the enum against the filter and producer sites: MsgHup, MsgBeat, MsgCheckQuorum, MsgUnreachable, MsgSnapStatus, MsgStorageAppend, MsgStorageAppendResp, MsgStorageApply and MsgStorageApplyResp are all locally produced and all listed; MsgProp, MsgApp, MsgAppResp, MsgVote, MsgVoteResp, MsgSnap, MsgHeartbeat, MsgHeartbeatResp, MsgTransferLeader, MsgTimeoutNow, MsgReadIndex, MsgReadIndexResp, MsgPreVote and MsgPreVoteResp are produced for or forwarded over the network and correctly unlisted; MsgForgetLeader is produced only by the two local ForgetLeader APIs and is unlisted, so it is the single exception.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution is claimed): the enum in raftpb, the isLocalMsg array in util.go, and every construction site for MsgForgetLeader found by searching the tree (rawnode.go, node.go, and the rafttest handlers, none of which put it on the wire). This bounds the earlier finding: the omission is a single-point classification gap, not a pattern.

knowledge.statement: A leader that stops hearing from a quorum steps down by itself: tickHeartbeat fires a MsgCheckQuorum step every election timeout when Config.CheckQuorum is set, and stepLeader responds to MsgCheckQuorum by calling ProgressTracker.QuorumActive (which treats each non-learner's RecentActive flag, reset for every peer but itself after each check, as a vote) and becoming a follower when that quorum is not active. So in a CheckQuorum deployment the coexistence of the incumbent and a leader elected at a higher term is bounded by an election timeout of the incumbent's own logical clock, not by how long the new leader's messages take to arrive.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution is claimed): raft.go 862-880 (tickHeartbeat's election-timeout branch dispatching MsgCheckQuorum), raft.go 1281-1294 (stepLeader's MsgCheckQuorum arm stepping down and clearing RecentActive for every peer but itself) and tracker/tracker.go 205-218 (QuorumActive over the voters' RecentActive flags) (set true on any peer message, cleared for all peers but the leader at each check). Applies only when Config.CheckQuorum is enabled; the bound was not measured in any receipt of this run, so it constrains the earlier receipts' scope rather than being witnessed by them.

knowledge.statement: A leader elected by a real vote among three equal-log voters, then advanced 20 ticks with no message delivered in either direction, was already StateFollower at the first CheckQuorum check (tick 10, its election timeout) and still a follower at tick 20, with its term unchanged at 2 throughout - so the module's own quorum check, not a peer's higher term, ended the leadership and it did so within one election timeout.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 45 and 46 of CheckRun 4393d47e3d51423390832c2b3d736512 (event s_leader_state at ticks=10 and ticks=20), with the pre-check state at the same receipt's s_leader_before event (ticks=0, StateLeader, term 2); config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum=true, PreVote=true, voters {1,2,3} from equal storage snapshots at index=10/term=1; nothing was delivered to the leader after the election, so this measures the silent case only.

knowledge.statement: A MsgReadIndex received by a leader that has not committed an entry in its own term is appended to pendingReadIndexMessages and answered only through releasePendingReadIndexMessages, which is called from a single site - the leader's append-response path once commit progress releases the queue - and which first requires committedEntryInCurrentTerm, otherwise it logs an error and leaves the queue intact. No other code path writes or clears the field: the search over the tree finds only the field declaration, the queueing site and that helper with its one call site, so a request queued before the node loses leadership is never cancelled; it is answered only if the same node again becomes leader and commits in a later term, in which case it is answered with the commit index reached at release time, and it otherwise stays unanswered.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution claimed): field declaration raft.go 428-435, queueing at raft.go 1361-1368, the release helper at raft.go 2127-2143 and its single call at raft.go 1548-1556. The caller contract that makes the unanswered case acceptable is node.go 218-224 (ReadIndex: 'request can be lost without notice, therefore it is user's job to ensure read index retries'). Not a defect finding; recorded because it bounds what the module guarantees about completion of an accepted read duty, and because a caller that assumed otherwise would retry unnecessarily - or not at all.

knowledge.statement: A leader elected with its append acknowledgement withheld has no commit in its own term, and a ReadIndex request issued then is accepted without producing any read state; once the follower receives that append and its acknowledgement is returned, the leader's commit advances to that index (with matches {1:11, 3:11} out of voters {1,2,3}) and the queued request is released as a read state carrying the index reached at release time and the original request context.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 48, 49 and 50 of CheckRun d7a20d42d5b84569a0c6e4924cd577a9; config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum+PreVote, ReadOnlySafe, voters {1,2,3} from equal storage snapshots at index=10/term=1, with node 2 never contacted so the quorum is exactly the leader plus node 3; the harness delivery helper writes each Ready's HardState and Entries to that node's MemoryStorage before Advance, which is the application duty the Ready contract states and without which this path cannot complete.

knowledge.statement: A read request queued by a leader that has no commit in its own term is not answered while that node loses leadership: after its own quorum check demoted it to follower at its old term, no read state had appeared for the request it still owed, and nothing answered it while it was not leader. When the same node led again at a higher term and committed an entry there, the stale request was released with the read index committed at that release time (12, where the index recorded at acceptance was 10) and with the request context it was accepted with.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 52 and 54 of CheckRun 478561f525b3471ca92b9aa20c6d12df; config ElectionTick=10, HeartbeatTick=1, CheckQuorum+PreVote, ReadOnlySafe, voters {1,2,3} from equal snapshots at index=10/term=1 with node 2 never contacted; the demotion came from the node's own CheckQuorum check, and the harness writes Ready entries to storage before Advance.

knowledge.statement: The regression is transient and self-healing. MaybeDecrTo's non-replicate branch lowers Next to max(min(rejected, matchHint+1), Match+1) and clears MsgAppFlowPaused, but while the progress is in StateSnapshot (a) the reject path in stepLeader calls BecomeProbe only for StateReplicate, so the state is unchanged, and (b) sendAppend returns immediately because IsPaused is true for StateSnapshot, so nothing is sent from the regressed value. Both ways out of StateSnapshot recompute Next from PendingSnapshot: a MsgSnapStatus without a rejection calls BecomeProbe with Next = max(Match+1, PendingSnapshot+1), and one with a rejection first zeroes PendingSnapshot and then calls BecomeProbe with Next = Match+1. So a stale rejection in that state at most logs a decrement, and the snapshot outcome restores a consistent Next; no probe from the wrong index and no stall follows.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution claimed): MaybeDecrTo at tracker/progress.go 226-261, BecomeProbe at 130-152, IsPaused at 262-278, the reject path at raft.go 1505-1520 and MsgSnapStatus handling at 1611-1624. The reachable trigger is a rejection for an append the leader sent before entering StateSnapshot, which under this source is the only way MaybeDecrTo sees rejected == Next-1 there.

knowledge.statement: The application-facing ordering duties are enforced by fatal guards, not by clamping: appending entries whose predecessor is below the commit index panics, committing to an index past the last index panics, reporting an applied index outside [previously applied, committed] panics, accepting application for an index past committed panics, and computing a non-positive application size budget panics. The only tolerated adjustments are non-fatal: applied-to bookkeeping clamps its outstanding-size counter at zero, and application is paused (applyingEntsPaused) once the outstanding size reaches the configured limit, resuming when the application's acknowledgement, via Applied or the storage apply response, brings the outstanding size down. Entry rewriting above the commit index is allowed by design, which is how a follower replaces a divergent uncommitted tail.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution claimed): log.go 136-140 (append guard), 322-328 (commitTo guard), 330-341 (appliedTo guard and counter clamp), 344-356 (acceptApplying guard and the pause condition), 234-238 (budget guard), with the client duties stated in node.go around ReadIndex/Ready and in the Ready struct documentation. The guards fire on values the module itself passes (from Ready/Advance) as well as on values an application reports in MsgStorageApplyResp, so a misreporting application is the party that trips them.

knowledge.statement: Step skips all term handling for a message whose term is zero, treating it as a local message, and then dispatches on its type: for MsgApp, MsgHeartbeat and MsgSnap that reaches stepFollower, which sets the election timer to zero and adopts m.From as the leader before handling the payload. So term-zero trust is not specific to MsgForgetLeader; what is specific to it is that it is the only locally-produced type missing from the inbound filter, so it reaches that trust from a peer with no illegal field at all, while a peer would have to send MsgApp or MsgHeartbeat with an illegal zero term to reach the same state change. That illegal-term path is not a correct-peer behaviour, its effect is bounded (a follower's advertised leader and timer, with a divergent uncommitted tail that the next real leader truncates) and it needs no classification change to be described.
knowledge.conditions: Captured snapshot, source reading only (no execution claimed): raft.go 1094-1100 (the term switch whose first case is the local-message case) and 1730-1739 (stepFollower setting electionElapsed and lead for MsgApp, MsgHeartbeat and MsgSnap). The contrast assumes a follower already at a term of at least 1, which every node reaches through becomeFollower(1, None) before it can lead or vote; the finding it clarifies is the main question's, whose evidence is the receipts cited there.

knowledge.statement: With a live leader already established from follower 2's point of view, a MsgHeartbeat from node 1 set its reported leader to 1, and a MsgHeartbeat of the same type from node 3 with no term field at all was accepted with no error and set the reported leader to 3; the follower therefore adopted a peer as leader on the strength of an illegal (unset) term rather than of a higher term.
knowledge.conditions: Observation indices 56 and 57 of CheckRun 2bb2e787750a4a799620f0b0d1673692 (event t_control_heartbeat with lead_after 1, and t_term0_heartbeat with term 0, step_error empty and lead_after 3, with the admission event t_setup carrying node 2, StateFollower, term 2, lead 0); voters {1,2,3} from equal snapshots at index=10/term=1 with CheckQuorum+PreVote, delivery through RawNode.Step, and the helper writing Ready entries to storage before Advance. The message is deliberately illegal for a peer to send: no correct producer emits a network-type message with the optional term field unset.

knowledge.statement: A peer-form MsgForgetLeader carrying a well-formed term acts exactly like the term-less form. With three real RawNodes (voters {1,2,3}, CheckQuorum+PreVote, equal logs at index=10/term=1) and follower 2 holding a live leader context at term 2, delivering MsgForgetLeader with From=3, To=2 and Term=2 through RawNode.Step returned no error and set SoftState.Lead from 1 to 0 (index 61 of CheckRun 5d829fd30b3649f8bb9ef79e6bb3d624); the identical pre-vote from the up-to-date candidate that the lease had withheld immediately before was granted immediately after (index 62), while the leader's real heartbeat had left Lead at 1 (index 59) and the same pre-vote under that live lease had produced no response at all (index 60).
knowledge.conditions: Follower is a voter holding a live leader context at the same term as the delivered message; sender is a real voter; Config.CheckQuorum and PreVote set; ReadOnlyOption is not ReadOnlyLeaseBased; the message is handed to RawNode.Step directly.

knowledge.statement: Step's term switch has cases only for a zero term, a higher term and a lower term, so a message whose term equals the receiver's own passes the whole term switch untouched and reaches the switch on its type; MsgForgetLeader has no case there either, so control lands in the default dispatch r.step(r, m), which for a follower is stepFollower, where the type sets r.lead = None whenever a leader is recorded and refuses only under ReadOnlyLeaseBased. The leader context is therefore cleared at the term the follower already holds, with no term comparison and no error, so the acceptance is a property of the missing classification rather than of the term field.
knowledge.conditions: Receiver is a follower; message type MsgForgetLeader; message term equals the receiver's own term or is zero; sender id is not checked for membership; ReadOnlyOption != ReadOnlyLeaseBased.

knowledge.statement: The snapshot's own tests do not pin IsLocalMsg(MsgForgetLeader) in either direction, and its inbound-path tests cannot detect a type missing from the filter. TestIsLocalMsg (util_test.go) enumerates every message type in the enum except one, listing all 23 types from MsgHup through MsgStorageApplyResp (the type numbered 22), and the single type every one of those entries omits is MsgForgetLeader, the last-numbered type (23). TestRawNodeStep steps a message of every type in MessageType_name through the real RawNode.Step and asserts ErrStepLocalMsg only when IsLocalMsg(msgt) is already true. TestNodeStep routes every type through the public node.Step and expects the receive channel to stay empty only when IsLocalMsg(msgt) is already true. Both tests read their expectation from the table under test, so neither would fail today for MsgForgetLeader, and neither would fail if the type were classified as local.
knowledge.conditions: Read from the captured snapshot as expectations, not executed in this run. RawNode.Step rejects a local-typed message with ErrStepLocalMsg when the sender is not a local thread id, whereas the public node.Step silently returns nil after ignoring it; the internal node.step path that node.ForgetLeader uses never passes through that check, which is why the two producers keep working either way.

knowledge.statement: The CheckQuorum leader lease is skipped when an incoming vote request carries the CampaignTransfer context marker. In Step, a MsgVote or MsgPreVote with a term higher than the receiver's own is ignored only when force is false and inLease holds, where force := bytes.Equal(m.GetContext(), []byte(campaignTransfer)) and inLease := checkQuorum && lead != None && electionElapsed < electionTimeout; with the marker present the receiver advances to the higher term and then evaluates canVote and isUpToDate, so a lease that is otherwise live suppresses nothing. The module attaches the marker only for a transfer campaign: campaign() sets Context = []byte(campaignTransfer) on every MsgVote request when t == campaignTransfer, the path reached from stepFollower's MsgTimeoutNow case, which calls r.hup(campaignTransfer); that campaign increments the term, sends MsgVote rather than MsgPreVote at the new term, and is the only producer of the marker. The receiving node keeps no local record of a pending transfer, so it cannot tell a real transfer from a claimed one; the marker is a statement about an internal precondition of the sender rather than about anything the receiver can verify.
knowledge.conditions: Config.CheckQuorum must be set, otherwise inLease is always false and the lease suppresses nothing; the receiver must be a follower holding a live leader context inside its election timeout; the marker only matters for MsgVote or MsgPreVote whose term exceeds the receiver's own; ReadOnlyOption is not involved.
